title: YAML 1.1 reads the `on:` key as boolean True, so pull_request_target workflows were never recognised as such
found: pwn-request test on a real-format workflow
detail: The analyzer looked up wf['on'] and got nothing, so the pull_request_target plus untrusted checkout check (the pattern behind several real CI compromises) silently never ran. Both the string and boolean spellings are read now.

title: Transposed-letter typosquats (lodahs, raect) were not flagged
found: typosquat test written from known squat patterns
detail: Plain Levenshtein counts an adjacent swap as distance 2, and the threshold was 1. A single adjacent transposition is now an edit.

title: Duplicate detection merged distinct bugs on the same asset and class
found: dedupe test against the synthetic corpus
detail: Comparing titles alone marked 22 of 40 reports as duplicates when only 4 were. Distinct bugs on one asset were being closed as dupes, which would have cost a reporter a payout and the program a fix. A duplicate must now share asset, class and endpoint.

title: Brand used as a subdomain of an unrelated domain was missed
detail: Only the registrable label was inspected, so sui.airdrop-claim.xyz scored 0. Every label left of the TLD is scanned now.

title: The digit 1 was read only as the letter l
detail: su1-rewards.xyz uses 1 for i. The skeleton now evaluates both readings.

title: Strong single drainer signals stayed under the detection threshold
detail: Unlimited approvals, eth_sign and misleading signing prompts scored 2 or 3 against a threshold of 4. Each is a decisive signal on its own and is weighted at the threshold.

title: A one-letter brand typo with no other signal, and the phrase 'limited time', raised false positives
detail: waltrus-electric.com and a newsletter signup were flagged. Typo-only matches now need corroboration and 'limited time' is no longer an urgency signal.

title: Rust parse_frame panics on short input
found: deterministic fuzz test (20000 cases) and explicit short-frame test
detail: Indexing without a length check panicked for any frame under 24 bytes, a remote crash for a service that parses network frames. The fix returns ParseError::TooShort.

title: Rust amount truncated with `as u32`
detail: A transfer of 2^32+5 units was booked as 5. The fix uses u32::try_from and returns LedgerError::Overflow.

title: Rust MAC comparison returned at the first differing byte
found: exploit test using bytes examined as a deterministic stand-in for timing
detail: Response time would reveal how many leading bytes of a MAC guess are right. The fix accumulates the difference over all bytes. The test proves equal work, not wall-clock timing.

title: TypeScript link preview fetched internal addresses (SSRF)
detail: Only startsWith('http') was checked, so cloud metadata, loopback, private ranges, file: and numeric hosts were fetched. A shared assertPublicHttps policy now applies.

title: TypeScript note renderer did not escape HTML (stored XSS)
detail: User text was interpolated into a template literal. The fix escapes & < > and quotes.

title: TypeScript session tokens came from Math.random
detail: Math.random is predictable from a few outputs. Tokens now come from crypto.randomBytes.

title: TypeScript transfer endpoint had no CSRF protection
detail: Cookie authentication alone let a cross-site form post move funds. A per-session CSRF token header is now required.

title: Variant analysis: the webhook sender had the same SSRF as INC-11
found: Semgrep taint rule derived from the INC-11 fix, swept over the whole target
detail: The INC-11 fix covered linkPreview only. The rule found notifyMerchant, which fetched a merchant supplied URL with the same weak check. Both now share one policy, which is the point of variant analysis: close the class, not the instance.

title: Move treasury withdraw had no capability check
found: Move access-control rule (pattern only, no Move toolchain)
detail: Anyone could call the public withdraw function and take funds. It now requires &AdminCap. The Move code was never compiled or run here.

title: Move rule flagged the real sui::coin test helpers
found: known-clean check on real Sui framework Move files
detail: &mut TxContext matched the shared-object argument pattern. It is excluded now. This is the known-clean check the posting asks for doing its job.

title: Rust slice rule flagged the already-fixed parser
found: known-clean check on the fixed Treasury sources
detail: The length guard sits inside an if, which the not-inside pattern did not recognise. A `if buf.len() < N` guard now suppresses the rule.

title: Release workflow combined pull_request_target, an unpinned KEV action, shell injection and a secret
found: GitHub Actions analyzer on the Treasury workflow
detail: Four critical or high findings on one file. The fix is tag triggered, pinned to a real commit SHA, passes the ref through env, scopes permissions, uses a protected environment and publishes with provenance.
